rows.title: The matrix ran with NO scene fingerprint, and its own artefacts show the drift #84 was refused for -- armed, measured, bounded
rows.evidence: #84 ran two cross-run A/B rounds and the second was REFUSED by sim.entities.live at a 6.5% population spread. Correct behaviour, and the matrix had no fingerprint at all. MEASURED FROM THE MATRIX'S OWN ARTEFACTS (two runs, 16 off-legs, harness/matrix/matrix-20260806-152507 and -153458): the worst |leg - baseline| population delta is 2.84%, and the SAME lever drifts in OPPOSITE directions between runs (backdropComposeMerge +0.24% then -2.84%; parallaxRefreshInterval +2.15% then -2.84%) -- so this is scene noise, not levers moving the population, which would have been a worse problem. #84's own scene explains its larger figure: it ran at bookmark 'explore', a procedural biome, which the 2026-08-06 sweep measured as the least stable class there is (19-21 entities, never settles, 'stable for only 1 of 90 required').
rows.impact: A leg's cost delta is (lever effect + scene difference) with nothing to separate them, and until now the population was neither recorded nor bounded -- so a reader could not even tell a clean leg from a drifted one after the fact.
rows.fixShape: ARMED. sim.entities.live is captured per leg, printed with its delta against that pass's baseline, carried into legs.tsv and the manifest, and legs past a 5% bound have costsQuotable set to no. The gauge is read as a LEVEL, not differenced -- and lighting.lights.sources was rejected as the fingerprint because it is a counter summed over frames, so a lever that changes frame rate would move it and the fingerprint would report the lever's own effect as a scene difference. Bound measured, not chosen: above the observed 2.84%, below the 6.5% #84 refused. The RESIDUAL -- systematic arm-vs-arm drift INSIDE the bound -- is O14, and its close is #84's in-process A/B.

signature.desc: the matrix runs with no scene fingerprint

rows.title: The two cache levers' declared output trade was ASSERTED, not certified -- and two of its clauses are refuted by the tree it describes
rows.evidence: AS ORIGINALLY FILED this row said the bound rests on the differential oracles that #136 records as blind, and that the replacement (a golden full-frame hash) was proven impossible by #191. BOTH PILLARS FAIL ON READING THE TREE. (1) The bound does not rest on those oracles: source/rendering/StarBackdropPass.cpp ORs an unconditionally-evaluated cadence term into the refresh predicate, so a refresh happens every N frames whatever the key does -- staleness is bounded by construction, and the ~12 env inputs absent from the content key are bounded by that term alone. The oracles certify a DIFFERENT property (refresh-frame fidelity), and the code says so itself: 'it claims nothing about the N-1 frames in between'. (2) #191's refutation is confounded -- see O12. SEPARATELY, scripts/lever-table.json carried two clauses the tree contradicts: 'snapped to {1,2,4,8,16}' (StarBackdropPass.cpp says 'No rung-snapping: any integer N is fine'; the harness has logged N=10, 13, 3, 6) and 'sub-ULP quantisation' (the oracle emits '<=~1 LSB expected: premult double-rounding' and render-gate.sh tolerates 1/255, the 8-BIT LSB -- a far weaker claim).
rows.impact: The matrix quotes a cost delta for each of these two levers against a stated trade. A trade stated in terms the instrument does not measure ('sub-ULP') and a derivation the code does not perform ('snapped') cannot be priced by the reader, and the bound that IS real was enforced by a single operand of a single call-site expression that no test constructed -- deleting it compiled clean and passed every gate.
rows.fixShape: Fold the cadence into RetainedSurface::shouldRefresh and make cadenceHit private, so no consumer can take the frame counter without the ceiling; assert the bound off-GPU in CI; and restate both `why` strings in terms of the mechanism that enforces the bound and the instrument that measures the delta. (Signature note: it points at the CONSUMER, not at retained_surface_test.cpp, because signature_matches skips every path containing '/test/' -- a signature aimed there can never match and would report the defect as permanently present.)

rows.title: #136 (PENDING) — the parallax baseline leg's adaptive N is clamped by a guard whose stated premise is false in the tree
rows.evidence: docs/board.md:1291-1293 (task #136, status pending): "FREE PERF NOT TAKEN: animated parallax layers always draw frame 0 (StarEnvironmentPainter.cpp:262-263), so the animation never advances and the parallaxAnimated -> clamp N<=4 guard protects nothing while costing cache efficiency. Left alone pending P-3 (#138)." Verified in tree: source/rendering/StarEnvironmentPainter.cpp:262-263 `if (layer.frameNumber > 1) first.subPath.emplace("0");` and source/rendering/StarBackdropPass.cpp:473-474 sets `parallaxAnimated = true` on `layer.frameNumber > 1`, then :485 `if (parallaxAnimated && parallaxAutoN > 4)` clamps.
rows.impact: scripts/lever-table.json pins parallaxRefreshInterval baseline=0 = ADAPTIVE, "the engine derives N per scene from layer drift rate, snapped to {1,2,4,8,16}". The baseline leg's cost therefore depends on a scene-dependent N that is silently capped at 4 whenever ANY parallax layer at the pinned location declares frameNumber>1 — a cap protecting an animation the renderer never advances. The measured saving is thus a function of the pinned location's layer manifest, not of the lever, and the table's `why` describes a derivation the code does not perform. Quoting the delta as "the parallax cache is worth X" is a name asserting one quantity over a value that means another.
rows.fixShape: Record the resolved N per leg in the matrix output (StarBackdropPass.cpp:492 already logs it) so the reader can see whether the baseline ran at 4 or 16, and either fix or delete the dead parallaxAnimated clamp.

rows.title: #226 H3 + the E04 unloadSector residual (recorded STILL OPEN inside a closed task) — a missed epoch bump inflates the witnesses of TWO matrix levers at once
rows.evidence: docs/board.md:4507+ (task #226): "H3 STILL OPEN, severity unverified. The cached transparency flags ... If the material database's render profiles change under a running client (asset reload), both the flags and the radiantLight results go stale with no tile write anywhere -- even a full re-gather reads the stale cached flags ... NEITHER the agent NOR I verified whether it invalidates m_gatherEpoch / m_gatherValid." and "ALSO RECORDED: unloadSector bumps no epoch either. Pre-existing, documented in the code, tracked as the E04 residual." Coupling verified in tree: source/game/StarWorldClient.cpp:2447 `bool sameGrid = m_gatherValid && m_gatherDims == calcDims && m_gatherEpoch == tileEpoch;` feeds the gather-hit outcome at :2392, and source/game/StarTemporalLightingGate.hpp:54 `if (tileEpoch != prev.tileEpoch)` drives the temporal skip counted at StarWorldClient.cpp:2262.
rows.impact: lighting.gather.hit is the declared WITNESS for lightingGatherCache and lighting.temporal.skipped is the declared WITNESS for lightingTemporalDecouple. Both read the SAME m_lightingTileEpoch. A bump that should have happened and did not makes the cache report a hit it did not earn and makes the temporal gate skip a recompute it should have done — so both witnesses read HIGH on the baseline leg for a reason that is a bug, not the lever. The witness moves, the leg certifies, and the quoted saving includes work that was skipped incorrectly. The board's own note is explicit that this is now MORE exposed since #225 removed the churn that was papering over it.
rows.fixShape: Answer #226's own small question (does m_lightingParamsReloadTracker's pullTriggered path drop the gather cache?) and either bump on unloadSector or declare mid-run sector unload / asset reload out of scope for the 94-minute window and assert it did not happen.

rows.title: #191 (PENDING) — four matrix levers declare changesOutput:false and nothing in the tree can certify that for the world body
rows.evidence: docs/board.md:3144-3148 (task #191, status pending): "VERIFICATION GAP, measured not just named: the golden full-frame hash CANNOT serve as the world-body oracle ... different hash every run ... #153 reached the same conclusion by another route. Making the world body reproducible means pinning entity animation phase at freeze; its own project." Against that, scripts/lever-table.json sets changesOutput:false for renderDrawableCache, renderVboOrphan, lightingGatherCache, scriptProtoCacheEnabled and backdropComposeMerge, each defended by a LOCAL argument ("a dedicated shadowCompare diagnostic", "byte-identical by construction", "proven algebraically", "documented as the original code path byte for byte").
rows.impact: changesOutput:false is the field that licenses quoting a lever's delta as a FREE win rather than a trade. Every one of those five claims is an instrument checked against itself — a per-subsystem shadowCompare, an algebraic argument, or a comment — with no whole-frame arbiter above them, and #191 records that the arbiter is not merely absent but demonstrably unbuildable in the current tree. If any of the five is wrong, the matrix reports a saving whose cost was paid in pixels nobody looked at.
rows.fixShape: Annotate the matrix output with the ACTUAL oracle backing each changesOutput:false claim (per-lever, by name), so "free win" is traceable to a specific check rather than to a boolean in a table.

rows.title: #75 (PENDING) — the scriptProtoCacheEnabled live toggle fix was never verified, and its witness is a call-site static that a steady-state window may never move
rows.evidence: docs/board.md:368-378 (task #75, status pending): "(1) Verify the same-session toggle FIX (commit f136c6b) ... check the new INFO log 'Lua Proto cache: ENABLED/disabled' confirms the flip ... If it logs 'disabled' after a true set -> config-persistence root cause to chase." Never done. In tree, source/game/scripting/StarLuaRoot.cpp:205-231: the enable flag is re-read only inside `if (protoCacheDirty)`, and BOTH witness counters (`script.proto.cache.loaded` :222, `.bypassed` :224) are function-local statics registered on the first call to loadContextScript, not at construction.
rows.impact: Two distinct exposures. (a) The board records an UNVERIFIED suspicion that the config write may not reach the live cache; if it does not, the off leg silently runs the ON path while the harness believes it flipped — the 2026-08-04 shape, both legs on the same arm. (b) Lua context loading is front-loaded at world load; if the telemetry window opens after load settles, both counters advance by ~0 on both legs, the runner reads IDENTICAL and voids the leg — which costs a slot in a 94-minute budget rather than producing a wrong number, but is the same root cause: nobody has watched this witness move.
rows.fixShape: Do #75 item (1) once before the run — set false, /serverreload, read the 'Lua Proto cache: disabled' log line — and confirm on a pilot capture that the counter delta is non-zero inside the window, not just non-zero cumulatively.

rows.title: #144 (PENDING) — the harness reads assets from the repo while the deployed game reads dev/opensb, and the renderVboOrphan lever's env override is silently dead
rows.evidence: docs/board.md:1608-1612 (task #144, status pending): "PROCESS TRAP (worth a script): the harness reads assets from the REPO (harness/sbinit.config points opensb at assets/opensb) while the live game reads ONLY dev/opensb + dev-feat/opensb. So the harness and the live game can run DIFFERENT SHADERS and the harness is the one that's right. A repo-only asset edit is a silent no-op in game." Same task, OUR OWN DEBT: "NoVboOrphan is a mutable file-scope global written by an instance method, not thread-safe." Verified: source/application/StarRenderer_opengl.cpp:26-29 initialises NoVboOrphan from getenv("STAR_NO_VBO_ORPHAN"), but source/client/StarClientApplication.cpp:537 calls `renderer->setVboOrphan(config->getOrDefault("renderVboOrphan").toBool())` on EVERY frame, overwriting it unconditionally.
rows.impact: Two ways. (1) Asset provenance: the matrix runs under the harness, so any lever whose off-value lives in an asset patch (the plantWindServerSkip precedent in assets/opensb/worldserver.config.patch) is measuring a shader/config set that is NOT what the Director's install runs — the number is real but is about a different binary+asset pair than the one it will be quoted against. (2) STAR_NO_VBO_ORPHAN is an INERT override: an operator who sets it to flip that lever gets the config value anyway, one frame later, with no error. That is the "config default that is inert or overridden" shape exactly, sitting on a lever that is in the table.
rows.fixShape: Assert at leg start that the harness asset tree matches the deployed one (the deploy-install.sh --verify #144 asks for), and either delete STAR_NO_VBO_ORPHAN or make setVboOrphan refuse to override an explicit env setting.

rows.title: #197 (PENDING) — persistent per-effect parameters are unasserted, and backdropComposeMerge changes the number of `world` effect binds between its two legs
rows.evidence: docs/board.md:3236-3270 (task #197, status pending): "EffectParameter::parameterValue (StarGlRenderSurface.hpp:30) is stored per effect and lives for the effect's lifetime. Nothing resets it at frame start; GlPass::bindEffect replays SCRIPTABLES only. So an ordinary parameter keeps whatever the last writer set, across frames and across consumers. THE EXPOSURE IS `world`: bound at TEN sites ... and declaring SEVEN parameters ... asserted by nothing." Verified in tree that the merge lever changes those bind sites: source/rendering/StarBackdropPass.cpp:378 and :570 call composeEnvStandalone (the OFF arm), which itself does switchEffectConfig("world") at :121 — an extra `world` rebind the merged arm at :654/:677 does not perform.
rows.impact: scripts/lever-table.json calls backdropComposeMerge "proven algebraically byte-identical" with changesOutput:false. That proof is about the compose ARITHMETIC; it does not cover the ambient effect-parameter state, which #197 records as persisting across frames and consumers with no frame-start reset and no assertion. The two legs execute a different sequence of `world` binds, so a parameter left stale by one arm and refreshed by the other is a live, untested difference sitting underneath a changesOutput:false claim — and #136's oracle-gap note says the differential oracles cancel exactly this class.
rows.fixShape: Do #197 option (b) — the debug-only draw-time check that every declared parameter of the bound effect was written this frame — and run one pilot leg of each arm with it armed before trusting the merge lever's changesOutput:false.

rows.title: The half of the cache levers' trade that IS uncertified -- refresh-frame fidelity across an FBO-lifecycle or ambient-GL-state change -- is in every existing instrument's null space
rows.evidence: envoracle/paralloracle build their reference from the SAME draw lambda at the SAME frame position under the SAME ambient GL state, and run ONLY on refresh frames, so an FBO-lifecycle event or a stale ambient parameter applies to both sides and cancels (#136, and BackdropPass says so at the call site). The in-process frozen A/B cannot substitute: on a frozen world the server is paused, Sky::update never runs and pinSkyEpochTime re-pins epochTime every frame, so EVERY term of both content keys is constant. Measured in the shipped gate's own log: 30 captured frames at envRefreshInterval=4 gave exactly ONE distinct frame hash, and envoracle fired exactly 8 times (=30/4, pure cadence). A stale cache is trivially correct there.
rows.impact: Not a wrong number -- a limit on what the matrix output may CLAIM. The cost delta for these two levers is valid; the accompanying 'not quality' half of the trade is uncertified for that one class, and both `why` strings now say so explicitly rather than implying full certification.
rows.fixShape: Drive the perturbation the oracles cancel: STAR_RENDERTEST_TOGGLE (a key whose change reallocates every framebuffer) and STAR_RENDERTEST_ZOOM already exist and are NOT gated on NOFREEZE -- renderTestDriveMotion is gated only on !m_renderTestLoading -- so they run under the frozen A/B today. What is missing is capturing WITHIN N frames of the perturbation rather than after each leg's full settle, and firing the in-frame comparison on SKIP frames scored against a staleness bound instead of exact equality.

rows.title: #191's golden-hash refutation was measured against a harness defect -- but MEASURING IT PROPERLY SUPPORTS ITS CONCLUSION, and names the term
rows.evidence: #191 ran 2026-07-26, nine days before 6e66f36e froze the render clock, so its runs were not frozen in the sense it assumed. Re-measured on the current binary with the sky clock AND both ray terms pinned (0c27d76b), at scenes chosen for the two preconditions nobody had ever characterised -- the world must SETTLE, and the sun must be up or the ray terms are inert. THE RESIDUAL TRACKS ENTITY POPULATION: at The Ark Ruins (an InstanceWorld, entities=1) five settled runs gave FOUR BYTE-IDENTICAL frames and one differing by a SINGLE PIXEL at ONE 8-bit LSB (worst maxAbs across all ten pairs = 1; null control of two same-hash runs = 0 differing pixels). At Desert Town (entities 267-271, parallaxLayers=34) five settled runs gave five distinct frames differing by 11-24% of pixels at maxAbs up to 255 -- INCLUDING the one pair whose entity COUNT matched exactly (268 vs 268: 18.78% of pixels, maxAbs 255).
rows.impact: Two corrections, in opposite directions. (1) The cross-run frame IS reproducible when there is no world body to be nondeterministic, so 'impossible' was too strong and the per-run backdrop terms this row originally named are worth about ONE PIXEL. (2) At any populated scene the frame is not reproducible at all, and no tolerance rescues it: 19% of pixels at full range is not a bounded difference. So #191's ATTRIBUTION -- per-entity animation phase, which nothing pins -- is supported by this data even though its evidence was confounded, and its 'its own project' sizing stands. A golden full-frame oracle for the WORLD PASS remains out of reach; a golden for a body-free scene is available today.
rows.fixShape: Do NOT pursue further backdrop determinism: it is measured at one pixel. If a world-body golden is wanted it needs entity animation phase pinned at freeze, which is #191's project and unstarted. What IS available now: a body-free instance scene reproduces to 1 LSB, so a golden there could gate the backdrop and compose paths -- and it must be scored as a BOUNDED diff (px count + maxAbs, tolerance 1 LSB) rather than by hash equality, because a hash has no tolerance and one LSB anywhere flips it. That is #223's defect exactly: 'paralloracle was never failing -- the gate read a BOUNDED-diff oracle as a zero-diff one.'

signature.desc: the harness no longer pins the sun-ray animation terms

rows.title: Quiescence gives WITHIN-run stability and was read as CROSS-run convergence; and which locations settle at all had never been characterised
rows.evidence: Measured across 8 bookmarks and ~20 runs. (a) SETTLING IS SCENE-DEPENDENT and the pattern is the opposite of the obvious one: authored places settle (Desert Town 273 entities YES, The Ark Ruins 47 YES) while sparse PROCEDURAL worlds never do (explore/exploring/Deep explore/Zerchesium, 19-21 entities, 'stable for only 1 of 90 required' -- the count changes almost every frame as monsters spawn and despawn around the player). (b) SETTLING IS NOT CONVERGENCE: five settled Desert Town runs froze at 268/268/271/267/270 entities, and the two runs that agreed on the COUNT still differed in 18.78% of pixels. (c) A dead teleport bookmark logs WARPING and never arrives, and the run captures wherever the player actually is: precursor-surface requested world ...91620126 and captured the previous location's fingerprint, silently.
rows.impact: Every cross-run render measurement this campaign has taken was at a scene nobody had checked against either precondition, and the default scene is whatever the player save happens to hold -- the harness inherits the persisted position, so the scene selects itself. 03-Surface Outpost, where all of today's early determinism work ran, fails BOTH: it never settles and it is at dayLevel=0, where the ray terms under test draw nothing.
rows.fixShape: Assert ARRIVAL, not just departure: after warping, refuse to capture unless the current world matches the bookmark's, so a dead marker is loud instead of silent. Put the world id in the [rendertest] fingerprint -- it is the one field that would have made both of today's arrival failures visible immediately instead of via dayLength archaeology. And record the settle/daylight character of the bookmarks a measurement is allowed to use, so scene choice stops being an accident of the save.

rows.title: A scene difference INSIDE the fingerprint's bound still corrupts a leg, and no repetition fixes it
rows.evidence: #84, having been refused at 6.5%, states the limit flatly: 'no number of repeated runs fixes a systematic arm-vs-arm population difference'. The bound armed in O01 catches gross drift; it cannot separate a lever effect from a 2% population difference that happens to fall the same way every pass. Interleaving and per-pass rotation reduce that risk; they do not detect it.
rows.impact: Cost deltas of the same order as the scene's own noise are not separable. It does not corrupt the matrix wholesale -- every leg now carries its population and its delta, so a marginal number is visible rather than silent -- but a small lever measured against a drifting scene is still a number whose name asserts more than its value means.
rows.fixShape: #84's own conclusion, and #153/GATE-1 proved the shape on the render side: an IN-PROCESS A/B that flips the lever between two measured windows within a SINGLE run, so both arms see literally the same world, the same entities and the same tick. Needs a per-lever check that each config key is safe to flip mid-run -- some are read per frame, some may not be -- before it is promised.

rows.title: render.drawable.cache.rekey.{version,generation,localtransform} register inside the renderDrawableCache ON arm — the lever's own diagnostics vanish on its OFF leg

The re-key attribution table (which key component drove the churn) is exactly the diagnostic the Director would read to interpret the renderDrawableCache cost delta, and it is unreadable on one of the two arms. rows.title: render.drawable.parts.rebuilt.rekey registers only inside rebuildStaticCache / the per-part cache — ABSENT on the renderDrawableCache OFF leg, breaking the documented `rebuilt - rebuilt.rekey` identity
rows.evidence: source/game/StarNetworkedAnimator.cpp:1048 (inside `rebuildStaticCache`, whose only caller is :981, itself below the `renderDrawableCache` early return at :935) and source/game/StarNetworkedAnimator.cpp:1107 (inside `drawablesWithZLevelPerPart`, gated by `renderDrawableCachePerPart` at :933, pinned FALSE at harness/storage-perf/starbound.config:555). Both are the only registration sites. Contrast: `render.drawable.parts.rebuilt` is also registered unconditionally at :928, so it survives — its partner does not.

On the off leg `rebuilt` is present (hoisted) and `rebuilt.rekey` is ABSENT. Any consumer performing that subtraction either raises KeyError or silently substitutes 0 — and cannot distinguish that from a leg where the metric was simply never wired in. The asymmetry (one operand present, one absent) is worse than both being absent, because it produces a number rather than a gap.

rows.title: lighting.gather.margin_cells registers only inside the SCROLL arm of the lightingGatherCache ON path — doubly unreachable on the off leg and at a pinned, parked camera
rows.evidence: source/game/StarWorldClient.cpp:2170, inside `WorldClient::shiftAndGatherMargin` (defined :2102). Its only call site is source/game/StarWorldClient.cpp:2460, inside `if (adx < calcDims[0] && ady < calcDims[1])` (the scroll arm), inside `if (configuration->get("lightingGatherCache").optBool().value(true))` at :2399. `lightingGatherCache` is lever #6 in scripts/lever-table.json (baseline true, off false).

rows.title: The measurement window's length is a snapshot-count lottery, and the end-trim RULE FLIPS below 4 snapshots — the leg that loses the trim is the one that ran slowest
rows.evidence: scripts/telemetry-window.py:282-283 — `lo = args.first if ... else (1 if len(files) >= 4 else 0)` / `hi = args.last if ... else (len(files) - 2 if len(files) >= 4 else len(files) - 1)`. render-profile.sh:238 invokes it with neither --first nor --last, so the defaults always apply. Verified against real captures: every leg in harness/matrix/matrix-20260806-152507/*.json has a `window` field spanning exactly ONE snapshot interval (e.g. ['telemetry-7431364.json','telemetry-7436227.json'] = 4863 ms), i.e. N=4 files → hi-lo = 1. One extra file (N=5) makes hi-lo = 2 and the window is exactly twice as long — that is the observed 600-vs-300-frame capture, and the legs.tsv witness `MOVED 0 300` for backdropComposeMerge confirms 300 = frames in a one-interval window.
rows.impact: Two things move at once. (a) Window length silently doubles between legs, so every windowed COUNT (the witness quantity, and every histogram bucket the p50/p99 are read off) is on a different scale between baseline and off leg with nothing recording that. (b) Worse, at N<=3 the trim rule inverts to lo=0: the first post-load snapshot — the one closest to the world load, deliberately trimmed at N>=4 for exactly that reason — is dragged INTO the window. So a leg that produced 3 snapshots is measured with load-adjacent, cold-cache data included while its baseline, which produced 4, is not. The A/B is then cold-vs-warm, not lever-on-vs-off, and nothing in the profile, the manifest or legs.tsv says which rule fired.
rows.fixShape: Pin the window explicitly: pass --first/--last (or a required --intervals N) from render-profile.sh, refuse the leg if fewer than N+2 snapshots exist, and record the chosen (lo,hi,intervals) into the profile JSON so lever-matrix.sh can assert every leg used the same window shape.

signature.desc: the window interval count is not declared

rows.title: Snapshot cadence is measured in SIMULATED time; the run length is measured in WALL time — so the snapshot count is lever-correlated, not random
rows.evidence: source/client/StarClientApplication.cpp:462 `float dt = GlobalTimestep * GlobalTimescale;` (a fixed timestep, not a wall delta) feeding StarClientApplication.cpp:519-521 `m_telemetryReportTimer += dt; if (m_telemetryReportTimer >= (float)interval) { m_telemetryReportTimer = 0.0f; ... writeSnapshot(...) }`, with harness/storage-perf/starbound.config:580 `"telemetryReportInterval": 5`. So a snapshot is emitted every exactly 300 update ticks. Meanwhile scripts/render-profile.sh:218 `sleep "$SECONDS_TO_RUN"` bounds the run in WALL seconds. The main loop (source/application/StarMainApplication_sdl.cpp:785-796) caps catch-up at `m_maxFrameSkip + 1`, so once a leg cannot hold 60 Hz the sim falls behind wall clock permanently.
rows.impact: This is what makes the previous finding fatal rather than merely noisy. A lever that costs CPU makes 300 update ticks take longer in wall time, so that leg fits FEWER snapshots into the same `sleep` — systematically, in the direction of the lever's own cost. The heaviest legs are therefore the ones most likely to fall to N<=3 and lose the load-adjacent trim, and the lightest legs get the longest, cleanest windows. The bias and the effect under measurement are the same variable.
rows.fixShape: Stop bounding the leg by wall clock. Either have render-profile.sh poll until a fixed COUNT of post-load snapshot files exists (then kill), or drive telemetryReportInterval off a wall clock in the engine — and in both cases write the achieved tick/wall ratio into the profile so a leg that fell behind is visible rather than inferred.

signature.desc: the leg is still bounded by wall clock, not snapshots

rows.title: The load-wait loop can time out silently, after which the measurement window straddles the world load

signature.desc: an unobserved world load does not fail the leg

rows.title: Leg order inside a pass is fixed and identical every pass, and there is no warm-up leg — so baseline is permanently the coldest slot and lever k permanently occupies the same thermal position
rows.evidence: scripts/lever-matrix.sh:431-479 — `for r in $(seq 1 "$REPEATS")` runs `run_leg "$BASE_LABEL"` first, then `for row in "${LEVERS[@]}"` in table order, and repeats that IDENTICAL sequence each pass. The header comment at lever-matrix.sh:373-376 claims interleaving handles this ("thermal state drifts over a multi-hour matrix, and consecutive repeats would bake that drift into whichever lever happened to run while the package was hot"). Nothing discards a first leg, and nothing warms or clears the on-disk shader cache (/root/.cache/mesa_shader_cache and /home/apnex/.cache/mesa_shader_cache both exist; neither render-profile.sh nor lever-matrix.sh mentions MESA_*, __GL_*, page cache or a governor pin — grep returns nothing).

Every baseline in the matrix runs on the coolest package and the lowest GPU clock of its pass, and every lever leg is compared against it — so every lever's delta carries the same one-signed warm-up offset, three times over, which averaging across repeats reinforces rather than cancels. The very first leg of the whole run additionally pays a cold shader cache and cold page cache; this project has already read a cold first run as a +47% instrument cost once.
rows.fixShape: Run and DISCARD one full warm-up leg before pass 1, and randomise (or rotate) the leg order within each pass so the baseline is not permanently in slot 0 — then assert from the sidecar that a leg's start clock/temp is within tolerance of its own pass's baseline.

signature.desc: no warm-up leg before pass 1

rows.title: The load phase is FRAME-capped, not time-capped, and the nofreeze path has no settle phase — so the window opens on a world that is by construction still streaming, for a lever-dependent amount of wall time
rows.evidence: scripts/render-profile.sh:146 `STAR_RENDERTEST_LOAD=${STAR_RENDERTEST_LOAD:-900}` and source/client/StarClientApplication.cpp:1305 `bool timedOut = m_renderTestFrame >= m_renderTestLoad;`. render-profile.sh's own comment at lines 155-159 states the live run "almost always" ends on the frame cap rather than on quiescence, and the engine logs that at Logger::error with "world did NOT settle" (StarClientApplication.cpp:1357-1363). The post-load settle phase (StarClientApplication.cpp:1384 `if (m_renderTestSeen < m_renderTestWarmup)`) is deliberately made unreachable by render-profile.sh:148 `STAR_RENDERTEST_WARMUP=100000000`.
rows.impact: 900 frames is a fixed amount of RENDER work, not a fixed amount of wall time, so a leg with a heavier lever spends longer in load — different amount of async chunk/entity streaming completed, different thermal state, different page-cache warmth at window open. And because the settle phase is disabled for the nofreeze instrument, the only warm-up discard in the entire pipeline is telemetry-window.py's `lo=1` trim, which is exactly the trim that disappears at N<=3. The leg is measured on an admittedly-unsettled world with a lever-dependent amount of settling behind it.
rows.fixShape: Add an explicit post-load settle in wall time (or in ticks) before the window opens — e.g. sleep a fixed settle period after the QUIESCED/did-NOT-settle line and BEFORE `rm -f "$SNAPDIR"/*.json` — and record the entity count and load-end frame into the profile so two legs can be shown to have opened on comparable worlds.

rows.title: m_renderTestLoading is not re-armed at the warp, so if the load phase ends before the warp fires the destination world streams in INSIDE the measured window
rows.evidence: source/client/StarClientApplication.cpp:1766-1785 — the warp block runs in updateRunning, is gated on `m_universeClient->worldClient()->inWorld()`, and on success sets only `m_renderTestFrame = 0;` (line 1775) with the comment "restart the LOAD phase from here". It does NOT set `m_renderTestLoading = true`, and does not reset `m_renderTestStable` / `m_renderTestLastEntities`. The load phase is exited unconditionally in renderTestCapture at StarClientApplication.cpp:1306-1310 once `m_renderTestFrame >= m_renderTestLoad` (900).
rows.impact: The `m_renderTestFrame = 0` reset only protects the case where the load phase is still running when the warp fires. If reaching inWorld() takes longer than 900 rendered frames, the load phase has already ended, the engine has already emitted the QUIESCED/did-NOT-settle line the harness polls for (render-profile.sh:163), and render-profile.sh then purges snapshots and opens its window — while the warp, the universe transition and a full destination-world load happen inside it. The stale m_renderTestStable also means a post-warp quiesce can be satisfied by stable-frame credit earned in the ORIGIN world. Nothing in the harness or the profile can distinguish such a leg from a clean one.
rows.fixShape: Set `m_renderTestLoading = true; m_renderTestStable = 0; m_renderTestLastEntities = 0;` alongside the m_renderTestFrame reset at the warp, and have render-profile.sh require the 'WARPING to bookmark' log line to appear BEFORE the QUIESCED/did-NOT-settle line.

rows.title: World and player state persist and mutate across every leg, with no snapshot, restore or assertion — the matrix drifts monotonically with leg index
rows.evidence: harness/storage-perf/starbound.config:493-494 `"clearPlayerFiles": false, "clearUniverseFiles": false`. render-profile.sh snapshots and restores ONLY the config (lines 114-121 `CFG_SNAPSHOT` / `restore_cfg`); nothing touches harness/storage-perf/universe/ or harness/storage-perf/player/. `ls -la` shows these are live: harness/storage-perf/player/555c692b...player and .../metadata and .../statistics all carry the timestamp of the last leg (Aug 6 15:58), and harness/storage-perf/universe/703931252_-540577323_-259783746_2.world was rewritten Aug 5 16:39 by a profiling run.

Leg N's ending state IS leg N+1's starting state, so the scene being rendered drifts monotonically across the ~30 legs of a 94-minute run. Because leg order within a pass is fixed, that drift maps onto lever identity, not onto noise. --warp pins WHERE the player stands; it pins nothing about what is standing there with them.

rows.title: The environment sidecar can silently emit invalid JSON, and even when valid nothing ever compares it between the two legs of a comparison
rows.evidence: scripts/render-profile.sh:203-207 `read_gpu_mhz() { cat /sys/class/drm/card*/gt_cur_freq_mhz 2>/dev/null | head -1 || cat .../cur_freq 2>/dev/null | head -1 || echo null; }` — a pipeline's exit status is `head`'s, which is 0 even when `cat` failed and produced nothing, so the `||` fallbacks and `echo null` are unreachable and the function returns EMPTY. Line 221-222 then interpolates that bare into a heredoc: `"gpuClockMhzEnd": $(read_gpu_mhz),` → `"gpuClockMhzEnd": ,`. scripts/telemetry-window.py:298-302 swallows the result: `try: meta.update(load(sidecar)) except (OSError, ValueError): pass  # a missing or malformed sidecar must never invalidate a real measurement`. The sidecar is written to `$SNAPDIR/../env-sidecar.json`, i.e. OUTSIDE the `rm -rf "$SNAPDIR"` at line 97, so a stale one from the previous leg survives. And no consumer compares gpuClockMhzStart/packageTempC across legs — telemetry-window.py:305-307 only prints them.
rows.impact: This is the one instrument built to check whether the ~7% run-to-run drift is thermal (its own comment, render-profile.sh:200-202, calls the current explanation "a guess"). It can be absent without a word, it can be the PREVIOUS leg's readings without a word, and even at its best it is a printed number with no tolerance and no gate — so a leg whose GPU clock differed from its baseline's by 40% is quoted exactly like one that matched. An instrument checked only against itself.
rows.fixShape: Make read_gpu_mhz/read_pkg_temp branch on captured output rather than on pipeline status (`v=$(cat ... | head -1); [ -n "$v" ] || v=$(...)`), delete the sidecar at the top of every run alongside the snapshot purge, validate the emitted JSON before the leg is accepted, and add a declared tolerance in lever-matrix.sh that VOIDs a leg whose start clock/temp differs from its own pass's baseline beyond that bound.

rows.title: The witness gate is an exact integer inequality with no tolerance — it survives only because every off-value in today's table happens to be exactly zero
rows.evidence: scripts/lever-matrix.sh:187 `print("MOVED %s %s" % (b, o) if b != o else "IDENTICAL %s %s" % (b, o))`, consumed at lever-matrix.sh:467-478 where MOVED = OK and IDENTICAL = VOID. Every witness in scripts/lever-table.json currently collapses to 0 on the off leg — harness/matrix/matrix-20260806-153458/legs.tsv shows `MOVED 225 0`, `MOVED 200 0`, `MOVED 45 0`, `MOVED 40508 0`, `MOVED 23194 0`, `MOVED 255 0`, `MOVED 40 0`, `MOVED 0 300`.
rows.impact: The gate exists to catch the 2026-08-04 shape (both legs ran with the lever off, a full table of plausible deltas, nothing objected). But `b != o` on two independently-sampled windowed counters is satisfied by noise alone — and given the window-length lottery above, a 300-tick baseline against a 600-tick off leg guarantees b != o for ANY nonzero counter, whether or not the lever engaged. The check reads as an assertion about the code path and is in fact an assertion that two noisy integers are not bit-equal. It is sound today only by luck of the current table's off-values; the first lever added whose witness merely reduces rather than zeroes will pass vacuously.
rows.fixShape: Declare the expected witness direction and magnitude per lever in lever-table.json (e.g. `"offWitness": 0` or a required fractional change), normalise both readings by their own window's tick count before comparing, and VOID on failure to meet the declared change rather than on bit-equality.

rows.title: Deep tracing is ON in the measured path and its cost scales with the event volume the levers change, so the instrument tax does not cancel in the A/B
rows.evidence: harness/storage-perf/starbound.config:577 `"telemetryDeepTracing": true`, read at source/client/StarClientApplication.cpp:357 `Telemetry::setDeepEnabled(configuration->get("telemetryDeepTracing", false).toBool());`. Every TelemetryScope then pays two clock reads per instance: source/core/StarTelemetry.cpp:258 `m_startMicros(Telemetry::deepEnabled() ? Time::monotonicMicroseconds() : -1)`. It cannot simply be turned off: the GPU timer queries are gated on the same flag (source/application/StarRenderer_opengl.cpp:1043 `if (!Telemetry::deepEnabled()) return;`). render-profile.sh's header (lines 12-18) enumerates what it turns OFF to avoid perturbing the measurement — the pixel oracles and vsync — and does not mention this one.
rows.impact: An A/B can tolerate a constant instrument offset because it cancels. This one is not constant: it is proportional to the number of scope entries, and several levers change that number by orders of magnitude (renderDrawableCache off moved its witness 40508 → 0; renderVboOrphan off moved 23194 → 0). So the off leg pays a different instrument tax than the baseline, and that difference is attributed to the lever. #172 measured the arming cost at +2.16% at one operating point; nothing establishes that it is the same +2.16% on both legs of a lever that multiplies the traced-call count.
rows.fixShape: Measure the deep-tracing tax on BOTH arms of at least the two draw-call-heavy levers (deep on vs deep off, same location), and either subtract the per-leg tax using the scope-entry counts already recorded, or state the residual as a declared uncertainty band on every quoted delta.

rows.title: The contention preflight runs once for the whole matrix, not once per leg
rows.evidence: scripts/lever-matrix.sh:327-331 — `if pgrep -x starbound >/dev/null 2>&1; then ... exit 1; fi` sits in the `=== lever matrix: preflight ===` block (line 319), before the plan is printed and before any leg runs. The per-leg integrity check inside run_leg (lever-matrix.sh:415) asserts only the config baseline; it does not re-check for a competing process. The comment justifying the check states the stakes exactly: "a second client competes for the same GPU, and every number this run produces would be contention."
rows.impact: A 94-minute unattended run is checked for GPU contention at minute 0 only. If the Director rejoins the game at minute 30 — or if any other GPU/CPU consumer starts — the remaining legs are measured under contention and the earlier ones are not, and legs.tsv/manifest.json record nothing that distinguishes them. Because leg order within a pass is fixed, a mid-run contention onset lands on a specific, identifiable subset of levers rather than spreading as noise.
rows.fixShape: Move the pgrep check into run_leg alongside assert_baseline, and additionally re-check after the leg completes, so a leg that started clean and finished contended is failed rather than quoted.

rows.title: All 13 GPU pass timers are declared MetricRole::Budget, but the code's own comment says they are NOT ADDITIVE and "do not budget"
rows.evidence: source/client/StarClientApplication.cpp:625-628 — "The per-pass GL_TIME_ELAPSED timers are NOT ADDITIVE -- with 12 of them their sum overshot the real frame by 5ms, because each bracket serialises the pipeline and measures its own stall. They rank passes; they do not budget them. The only trustworthy figure is the whole-frame span." Yet every one of the 13 begin() sites declares MetricRole::Budget: StarRenderer_opengl.cpp:1186 (clear), :1873 (blit), StarClientApplication.cpp:640 (interface), StarWorldPass.cpp:56 (world), StarBackdropPass.cpp:117, :255, :321, :578, :624, :668, StarWorldPainter.cpp:323, StarGpuLightmapPass.cpp:151, :243, :308, :327. MetricRole::Budget is defined at source/core/StarTelemetry.hpp:43-44 as "a part; sums with its siblings and must close against the owner's Total." scripts/telemetry-window.py:374 does exactly that: `parts = sum(scaled[k][0] for k,v in rows if v["role"]=="budget" and v["domain"]==dom)`, closed against render.frame.gpu_span_us (source/core/StarTelemetry.cpp:441).
rows.impact: The gl/gpu "accounted" percentage the matrix prints per leg is a sum of quantities the repo itself documents as non-summable, because each GL_TIME_ELAPSED bracket serialises the pipeline and charges its own stall to itself. The number therefore over-counts by an amount that depends on how many brackets happened to open that leg — and a lever that changes which passes run (envRefreshInterval, parallaxRefreshInterval, backdropComposeMerge all do) changes the bracket count between baseline and off leg, so the closure delta is partly an artefact of the instrument. This is the un-named root cause behind #236's "parts can exceed the whole": the parts were never a partition. The correct declaration for a rank-only instrument is Detail (excluded from sums), or the closure must be computed from ablation deltas as line 628 prescribes.
rows.fixShape: Either demote all 13 gpu_us pass timers to MetricRole::Detail (they rank, they do not close), or keep Budget and make the gl/gpu closure explicitly a rank table with no summation — but do not let a sum of self-stalling brackets be printed as a budget closure.

signature.desc: a gpu-domain descriptor still declared Budget

rows.title: lighting.gpu.point.gpu_us declares Cadence::Recompute but its bracket sits inside `if (!lights.empty())`
rows.evidence: source/rendering/StarGpuLightmapPass.cpp:240-243 — `if (!lights.empty()) { m_renderer->switchEffectConfig("lightingPoint"); m_renderer->gpuTimer().begin("lighting.gpu.point.gpu_us", MetricDesc{MetricDomain::Gpu, MetricOwner::Gl, MetricCadence::Recompute, MetricRole::Budget});` — end at :292. The identical defect was already diagnosed and fixed twice elsewhere in this repo with an explicit rule: source/rendering/StarWorldPainter.cpp:315-317 ("Bracket INSIDE the gate, Cadence::Call ... A pass that did not happen has no cost to report") and source/application/StarMainApplication_sdl.cpp:746-754 (cpu.frame.idle.us, Frame->Call, "parts exceeding their own whole").

On any recompute with no point lights the bracket does not run, so coverage < 1 and scripts/telemetry-window.py:201-202 divides this Budget part's total by that coverage — inventing GPU cost for recomputes on which the pass genuinely did not execute, and pushing owner `gl` parts above its whole. rows.title: lighting.gpu.upscale.gpu_us declares Cadence::Recompute but its bracket is inside a config-gated arm that is off by default
rows.evidence: source/rendering/StarGpuLightmapPass.cpp:318 `if (worldUpscale >= 1.5f && m_renderer->switchEffectConfig("lightingUpscale")) {` ... :326-327 `m_renderer->gpuTimer().begin("lighting.gpu.upscale.gpu_us", MetricDesc{MetricDomain::Gpu, MetricOwner::Gl, MetricCadence::Recompute, MetricRole::Budget});` ... end :331. worldUpscale comes from the `lightingWorldUpscale` config read at source/rendering/StarWorldPainter.cpp:300-301. The `else` arm at :332-336 is the ungated path.

If the config is below the threshold the key is never registered at all (GPU keys register lazily inside GlGpuTimer::begin's readback at StarRenderer_opengl.cpp:1078), so the Budget part reads ABSENT, not ZERO. Either way a per-leg gl closure number changes for reasons unrelated to the lever under test.

rows.title: render.frame.blit.gpu_us declares Cadence::Frame, but the blit has no once-per-frame guard AND the timer is silently dropped by the nesting guard
rows.evidence: source/application/StarRenderer_opengl.cpp:1871-1873 declares `MetricCadence::Frame`. Twelve lines above, :1861-1863: "NOTE the missing once-per-frame guard. Upstream deliberately dropped the `if (blitted) return;` ... the alt->primary copy must happen on EVERY effect switch, not once per frame". The sole caller is switchEffectConfig at :535, invoked once per post-process effect per frame (source/client/StarClientApplication.cpp:609-616 loops layers x passes x effects) plus the interface switch at :618. And the nesting guard at :1057-1065 records the consequence explicitly: "This bit immediately: the blit timer fires INSIDE the interface timer (blitGlSurface is reached during the interface render), and the resulting numbers were nonsense" — begin() returns early at :1066-1068 when m_active.
rows.impact: The declared cadence says count == frames. The actual count is (number of effect switches that blit) minus (all of those that occurred while any other pass bracket was open), which is neither frames nor blits and varies with how many post-process effects are enabled. As a Budget part under owner `gl`, whatever survives is coverage-scaled by telemetry-window.py against the frame count and then summed into the gl closure. Simultaneously, the blit time that WAS suppressed is still physically inside render.pass.interface.gpu_us, so it is double-jeopardy: under-counted here, silently billed there. The matrix cannot attribute any gl-domain delta between legs while this part's denominator is unknowable.
rows.fixShape: Declare render.frame.blit.gpu_us MetricCadence::Call, and count the nesting-guard rejections per key (the guard at :1066 currently only warns) so suppressed samples are visible rather than inferred.

rows.title: The same event is declared Call by one timer and Recompute by four others, 55 lines apart in one function
rows.evidence: source/rendering/StarGpuLightmapPass.cpp:91-96 — lighting.gpu.cpu_cost.us is declared `MetricCadence::Call` with the reason spelled out: "Cadence::Call, not Frame: processFull is reached only inside `if (lightMapUpdated)` (StarWorldPainter.cpp), so it fires on lightmap-publish frames, not every frame." Its TelemetryScope opens at :101 and covers the whole function. The four GPU brackets inside that same scope — :151 spread, :243 point, :308 compose, :327 upscale — all declare `MetricCadence::Recompute`, asserting count == lighting.temporal.recomputed. lightMapUpdated is `lightWaiter()` (source/rendering/StarWorldPainter.cpp:254), i.e. one render-thread consumption of a publish; lighting.temporal.recomputed is incremented on the lighting thread at source/game/StarWorldClient.cpp:2301.
rows.impact: One invocation event cannot legitimately be Call for the CPU timer and Recompute for the GPU timers that live inside it — they fire exactly once each per processFull call. Whichever is right, the other's number is wrong: if publishes and consumptions are 1:1 then cpu_cost.us is silently forgoing its coverage check; if they are not 1:1 (frame skip runs update 1..N times per rendered frame — StarMainApplication_sdl.cpp:786-790 — so multiple publishes can coalesce into one consumption) then all four GPU passes are coverage-scaled up by a factor nobody has measured, straight into the gl closure. Nothing in the tree asserts the two counts agree, so this is an instrument checked only against itself.
rows.fixShape: Register a counter for processFull invocations and assert it equals lighting.temporal.recomputed over a window; then make all five descriptors in the function agree on one cadence.

rows.title: animator.{state,part}.merge.* declare MetricOwner::Sim but the counters are incremented on the client render path and read as a client HUD statistic
rows.evidence: source/base/StarAnimatedPartSet.cpp:288-291 and :351-356 declare five counters with `MetricOwner::Sim`. AnimatedPartSet::update is driven by NetworkedAnimator::update (source/game/StarNetworkedAnimator.cpp:1612), which runs for client-side slave entities as well as server-side masters. source/client/StarClientApplication.cpp:659-668 reads all four merge counters and publishes them as `telemetry_animator_state_skiprate` / `telemetry_animator_part_skiprate` on the client's own telemetry HUD.
rows.impact: One counter aggregates two budgets. A Sim-owned number that is partly Frame work cannot be attributed to either owner, which is #171's shape in a second subsystem: any per-leg movement is un-splittable between the server tick and the client frame, so it cannot be used to explain a delta in either owner's table. Impact is bounded today only because these are MetricRole::Detail counters and scripts/telemetry-window.py:316 restricts owner tables to `type == "timer"` — they never enter a closure. They are still labelled by an owner that does not do all the work.
rows.fixShape: Split into client/server keys or declare MetricOwner::Unknown rather than asserting Sim; at minimum document at the registration that the value spans two budgets.

rows.title: render.glstate.mismatches declares Cadence::Frame but its value is a count of mismatched state items, incremented only on frames that already failed
rows.evidence: source/application/StarRenderer_opengl.cpp:95-96 declares `MetricCadence::Frame`. The only increment is source/application/StarRenderer_opengl.cpp:1253 `m_glStateMismatches.inc(bad);` inside `if (bad)` at :1252, where `bad` is a sum over the pass audit plus the scissor and blend checks (:1222-1250) and can be 0, 1, 2 or more per frame.
rows.impact: Cadence::Frame asserts the count is checked against the frame count (StarTelemetry.hpp:33-35). This value is neither per-frame nor a frame count — it is a per-frame SUM of defects, zero on healthy frames. Nothing consumes it today (counters are excluded from telemetry-window.py's owner tables at line 316), so no matrix number moves; but the cadence field on this metric is an assertion no reader can act on, and the counter's own registration comment at :91-94 is careful about ABSENT-vs-ZERO while the cadence is not.
rows.fixShape: Declare MetricCadence::Call — errors are exceptional and not per-anything, exactly the reasoning already written for render.gl.errors at StarRenderer_opengl.cpp:1619-1621.

rows.title: Renderer-internal CPU counters split between MetricOwner::Frame and MetricOwner::Gl within one file, including a lever WITNESS
rows.evidence: In source/application/StarRenderer_opengl.cpp: render.glstate.mismatches is `MetricOwner::Gl` (:96) while render.vbo.orphaned (:1502), render.flush.count (:1727) and render.flush.primitives (:1729) are all `MetricOwner::Frame` — all four are OpenGlRenderer-internal CPU work in the same translation unit. render.vbo.orphaned is the declared witness for the renderVboOrphan lever (scripts/lever-table.json, witness field).
rows.impact: Owner is the budget a cost lands in, and these four land in the same one. Declaring the same subsystem two different owners means any future promotion of one of them to Budget puts it in the wrong closure. Today all four are MetricRole::Detail counters and counters do not enter telemetry-window.py's per-owner timer tables, so no matrix number is currently wrong — but the witness for a live lever is filed under an owner its work does not belong to, which is a misreading waiting to happen when someone asks which budget the renderVboOrphan lever moved.
rows.fixShape: Pick one owner for OpenGlRenderer-internal CPU counters (Gl, matching the file's own render.glstate.mismatches) and apply it to all four.

rows.title: lighting.cells / lighting.calc.cells declare Cadence::Call while every sibling lighting metric declares Recompute
rows.evidence: source/base/StarCellularLighting.cpp:99-102 declares both gauges `MetricCadence::Call`; they are set inside CellularLightingCalculator::begin, which is reached only from the lighting recompute path (source/game/StarWorldClient.cpp:2238-2239 brackets it as lighting.cpu.begin.us, itself declared MetricCadence::Recompute at :2239).
rows.impact: The metric fires exactly once per recompute but declares no cadence expectation, so it forgoes the coverage/bounds check that its co-located timer gets. No number is scaled wrongly (gauges carry the latest reading — scripts/telemetry-window.py:133 — and are not coverage-scaled), so this under-declares rather than misstates. It matters because lighting.calc.cells is the scene fingerprint used to prove two legs saw the same world; a fingerprint with no declared cadence cannot be checked for having been sampled the expected number of times.
rows.fixShape: Declare both MetricCadence::Recompute to match the phase they are set inside.

rows.title: serverFidelity is left on "automatic" in the pinned harness config — a negative-feedback governor that changes the simulated WORKLOAD between legs, and whose level never reaches telemetry
rows.evidence: harness/storage-perf/starbound.config:420 `"serverFidelity" : "automatic"`. source/game/StarWorldServerThread.cpp:213-216 reads it and leaves `lockedFidelity` unset for "automatic". The code's own comment at :295-300 states the prerequisite verbatim: "serverFidelity defaults to 'automatic' ... so this is ALWAYS live unless the Director pins it -- and it is negative feedback on precisely the quantity the total measures: a slower tick lowers fidelity, which makes the next tick cheaper. Any A/B on owner `sim` must therefore either pin serverFidelity or report the fidelity level alongside the delta, or it is measuring the governor's response rather than the change under test." The fidelity level is published ONLY to the on-screen debug map (StarWorldServerThread.cpp:264 `LogMap::set(strf("server_{}_fidelity", ...))`) — grep finds no Telemetry counter/gauge for it, so no snapshot can say what level a leg ran at. It is not a cosmetic dial: StarWorldServer.cpp:872 gates phases on a "fidelity-driven cadence gate", :918 sets the liquid engine's processing limit from m_fidelityConfig, :942 sets the world-storage generation limit.
rows.impact: The matrix runs client-side render levers in a single process that also hosts the server thread, both inside `taskset -c 6-15 nice -n 19` (render-profile.sh:145-149). A lever that frees CPU hands it to the server thread; spareTime rises; fidelity increments; more liquid cells, more entity phases, more sectors generate. The OFF leg and the baseline leg then render DIFFERENT SCENES, and every counter moves together — which is exactly the #84 failure the fingerprint refused ("Every control moved the same way ... The win was the scene"). None of the 42 findings names the governor: the sweeps covered thermal position, contention, world-file drift and snapshot cadence, but not the in-process feedback loop between client cost and simulated workload. Worse, because the level is LogMap-only, a leg cannot even be retrospectively disqualified — there is no record of what fidelity it ran at.
rows.fixShape: Pin `serverFidelity` to a named level in harness/storage-perf/starbound.config, add it to lever-table.json's asserted-baseline set so a drift is fatal, and register the live level as a gauge so every leg's snapshot states it.

signature.desc: the matrix does not pin/assert serverFidelity (harness config is gitignored, so the enforceable half is the pinned map)

rows.title: The asset set — the measurement's content input — is 42 unrecorded paths outside the repo, one of them a live mod tree belonging to an in-progress task, with digest checking explicitly disabled and no asset identity anywhere in the manifest
rows.evidence: harness/sbinit-perf.config lists 42 `assetSources`: `/home/apnex/OpenStarbound/assets/packed.pak`, `/root/frackin/OpenStarbound/assets/opensb`, `/home/apnex/base-in-a-box-reforged/mod`, and 39 Steam Workshop `contents.pak` files under `/home/apnex/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/workshop/content/211820/`. The same file sets `"assetsSettings": {"digestIgnore": [".*"]}`, and harness/storage-perf/starbound.config:342 sets `"checkAssetsDigest" : false`. `/home/apnex/base-in-a-box-reforged/mod` exists and holds 282 files; it is the working tree of task #130, status in_progress. lever-matrix.sh's manifest writer (scripts/lever-matrix.sh:485-497) emits runId, warp, repeats, secondsPerLeg, leverTable, legs and an analysis note — no asset list, no digest, no mtime. The env sidecar (render-profile.sh:203-212) records GPU clock and package temperature only.
rows.impact: Each leg is a fresh process that re-reads the asset chain at startup, so any edit to any of the 42 sources between leg N and leg N+1 silently changes the world content, the entity set and the material render profiles the next leg measures — and one of those sources is a directory somebody is actively developing in. digestIgnore ".*" plus checkAssetsDigest:false remove the one mechanism that would have noticed. Because nothing records what the assets WERE, a 94-minute matrix produces numbers that cannot be reproduced, cannot be compared to any future run, and cannot be retro-attributed to a content state. This is the #226-H3 hazard ("if the material database's render profiles change under a running client") arriving through the front door, and no sweep touched the assets dimension at all.
rows.fixShape: Hash the resolved asset chain (path + size + mtime, or the real digest) once in the matrix preflight, write it into the manifest, and re-assert it before every leg so a mid-run content change aborts instead of landing as a delta.

signature.desc: the asset chain is not fingerprinted

rows.title: Neither render-profile.sh nor lever-matrix.sh asserts the binary is newer than the sources — the check the repo already wrote for render-gate.sh — and the manifest records no commit or binary identity at all
rows.evidence: scripts/render-profile.sh:61 is the entire binary check: `[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "no $BIN -- build first"; exit 1; }`. scripts/lever-matrix.sh:323 is the same: `[ -x dist/starbound ] || { echo "lever-matrix: no dist/starbound -- build first" >&2; exit 1; }`. Contrast scripts/render-gate.sh:96-106, which does exactly what is missing: `stale=$(find source -path source/test -prune -o -type f ... -newer "$BIN" -print ...)` then `REFUSING TO CERTIFY: these sources are newer than $BIN -- the build never ran, or it FAILED`. Its header at :85-95 names the defect class ("a FAILED BUILD satisfies trivially: the compile errors out ... Every byte-identity claim made through here inherits that hole. #178"). `grep -n 'git rev-parse\|commit' scripts/render-profile.sh scripts/lever-matrix.sh` returns nothing, and the manifest written at lever-matrix.sh:485-497 carries no SHA, no binary hash, no binary mtime. The snapshot's own meta carries only `{"schema": 3}` (StarTelemetry.cpp:508) plus `vsync` (StarClientApplication.cpp:523).
rows.impact: A failed or forgotten build leaves dist/starbound untouched, so a 94-minute matrix can run entirely against a binary that predates the levers, the counters, or the descriptor-convergence work now in flight. The witness gate catches only the narrow case where a lever key is absent from the binary (the OFF leg then reads identical to baseline and VOIDs that one leg); every other leg, including the baseline whose cost is the reference for all eight comparisons, passes silently while describing a different tree. And because nothing records which binary produced the numbers, the run cannot afterwards be tied to a commit — the matrix's output is unattributable by construction, which is the one property the Director's "perfectly closed" standard cannot tolerate.
rows.fixShape: Lift render-gate.sh:96-106's staleness find into the lever-matrix preflight, and write `git rev-parse HEAD`, the binary's sha256 and its mtime into the manifest and into every leg's profile JSON.

signature.desc: the matrix preflight does not assert the binary is current

rows.title: gputimer-brackets.py — the gate that exists to stop a GPU timer bracketing a gate it does not enter — fires only on one syntactic shape and never reads the declared Cadence it tells you to fix
rows.evidence: scripts/gputimer-brackets.py:72-74: after taking the first non-blank body line, `if not re.match(r'^\s*(if|else\s+if)\s*\(', first): continue`. Any statement before the gate, or a loop-shaped gate, exits the detector. Executed against the live module (read-only, in-memory): a body of `auto size = camera.screenSize(); if (refresh) { drawIt(size); }` inside the bracket returns `[]`, and `for (auto const& l : lights) { drawLight(l); }` inside the bracket returns `[]`, while the module's own DIRTY fixture returns `[('D', 5, 'render.pass.x.gpu_us')]`. Separately, check() at :180-196 reads only begin/end positions — it never parses the MetricDesc, although its own failure message ends "and declare MetricCadence::Call" and its docstring rule at :22-24 states "the bracket opens INSIDE the gate, AND the metric is Cadence::Call". The four selftest fixtures (:106-158) all use the bare-`if` shape, so the blind spot is not exercised.
rows.impact: This is the gate for the exact failure this project is calibrated on — "a GPU timer bracketing a conditional it did not enter, so it timed nothing and reported a mean". It certifies only the one shape that has already been fixed. A zero-iteration loop records an empty bracket identically to a skipped `if`, and one hoisted local above the gate makes the original 4.04x defect invisible again. It is also why findings #2 and #3 are green under it: both are brackets correctly nested inside a gate but declared Recompute rather than Call, and the gate never looks at the declaration half of its own rule. A green gate here is currently evidence about grep shape, not about the tree.
rows.fixShape: Extend violations() to treat any leading statements plus a body-spanning `if`/`for`/`while` as the gated shape, and add a second arm that parses the MetricDesc at the begin site and fails a gated bracket not declared Cadence::Call — with selftest fixtures for the hoisted-local and empty-loop shapes.

rows.title: The engine emits descConflict/typeConflict on every metric and NOTHING in the tree reads them; the plan that specified the consumer assigned that oracle to telemetry-window.py, where it does not exist, and owner-"unknown" rows are silently dropped from the report
rows.evidence: source/core/StarTelemetry.cpp:494-495 puts `descConflict` and `typeConflict` into every metric object in every snapshot. `grep -rn 'descConflict|typeConflict' scripts/` returns nothing; scripts/telemetry-window.py:126 forwards exactly `("type", "domain", "owner", "cadence", "role")` and drops both flags, and `grep -n 'UNDECLARED|CONFLICT|conflict'` over the whole file returns nothing. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-25-unified-telemetry-model.md:1451-1457 removed the C++ oracle on purpose ("core_tests never registers the game's metrics ... reset() clears the conflict flags, so ... It could never fail") and reassigned it: "The **real** conflict oracle must run against a snapshot captured from a real client run ... that is Task 4 Step 4's UNDECLARED/CONFLICTS check and the violation reporting in telemetry-window.py (Task 8). Both must additionally check typeConflict, not just descConflict." That step is still an unchecked box. Compounding it, telemetry-window.py:323 filters owners with `if m.get("owner") not in (None, "unknown")` — and MetricOwner::Unknown is the default (source/core/StarMetricDesc.hpp:47) — so an undeclared metric leaves the report with no diagnostic and no count.
rows.impact: applyDesc (StarTelemetry.cpp:47-58) is FIRST-DECLARATION-WINS: when two call sites declare one key differently, the snapshot keeps the first descriptor, sets the flag, and the consumer throws the flag away. The number then carries a descriptor that only one of its two producers agreed to — precisely "a name asserting one quantity while the value means another" — and the only instrument that knows is discarded in transit. Findings #5 (Call vs Recompute for one event, 55 lines apart) and #8 (Frame vs Gl within one file) are exactly this class; the flag that would have named them mechanically was already on the wire. This is the snapshot-writer modality: the sweeps read declarations at the call sites, but nobody checked whether the writer's own self-diagnostics survive to the consumer. The owner-"unknown" filter is the same defect one layer down: absent rather than flagged.
rows.fixShape: Have telemetry-window.py collect any metric with descConflict, typeConflict, or owner/domain "unknown" into `violations`, so a conflicted or undeclared key exits 3 and lands in the manifest's costsQuotable=no column instead of vanishing.

rows.title: Finding #23's mechanism is contradicted by the tree: the main loop paces update() to WALL time, so snapshot cadence is not lever-correlated the way claimed — the real hazard is the maxFrameSkip clamp, and it points the other way
rows.evidence: Finding #23 asserts "Snapshot cadence is measured in SIMULATED time; the run length is measured in WALL time — so the snapshot count is lever-correlated". The tree closes that loop. source/application/StarMainApplication_sdl.cpp:783-785 drives update() from wall-clock lag: `int updatesBehind = max<int>(round(m_updateTicker.ticksBehind()), 1); updatesBehind = min<int>(updatesBehind, m_maxFrameSkip + 1);` and :841-845 gives back the surplus: `int64_t spareMilliseconds = round(m_updateTicker.spareTime() * 1000); if (spareMilliseconds > 0) { TelemetryScope s(tIdle); Thread::sleepPrecise(spareMilliseconds); }`. The target rate is the sim rate (source/client/StarClientApplication.cpp:303 `float updateRate = 1.0f / GlobalTimestep;`, :312 `appController->setTargetUpdateRate(updateRate);`) and GlobalTimescale is 1.0f (source/game/StarGameTypes.cpp:5). So accumulating a fixed `dt` per update (StarClientApplication.cpp:463, 519-521) advances at one wall second per second, and telemetryReportInterval=5 (starbound.config:428) means ~5 wall seconds per snapshot on every leg. The genuine residual is the OPPOSITE case the finding does not name: the `min(..., m_maxFrameSkip + 1)` clamp (default 5, StarMainApplication_sdl.cpp:1423) means a leg that cannot sustain the update rate DROPS sim time, so simulated time — and therefore snapshot cadence — stretches only on the SLOWEST legs.
rows.impact: A prerequisite list is an instrument too, and a wrong entry costs the Director the same as a missing one: acting on #23 as written would harden a mechanism that is already closed while leaving the real one — saturation-induced snapshot stretch on exactly the legs that ran slowest — unnamed and unmeasured. That residual is the one that biases the window, because it is correlated with lever cost in a direction nobody is watching for. No sweep opened the main loop, so both the refutation and the real hazard were missed.
rows.fixShape: Re-scope #23 to the maxFrameSkip clamp, and have each leg assert `cpu.frame.updates` delta against elapsed wall seconds × updateRate — a shortfall means the leg dropped sim time and its window is not the length it claims.

rows.title: cpu.frame.total.us — the declared Total and the owner-frame denominator — is a wall-clock pacing period that deliberately contains a sleep, and the sleep is itself declared a Budget part
rows.evidence: source/application/StarMainApplication_sdl.cpp:728-734 declares `cpu.frame.total.us` as `MetricRole::Total` with the comment "THE FRAME BUDGET. cpu.frame.total.us is the denominator for owner=frame", and StarTelemetry.cpp:431/440 wire it as both the MetricOwner::Frame denominator and its Cpu-domain whole. StarMainApplication_sdl.cpp:754-756 declares `cpu.frame.idle.us` as `MetricDomain::Cpu, MetricOwner::Frame, MetricCadence::Call, MetricRole::Budget` — and its scope at :844 wraps `Thread::sleepPrecise(spareMilliseconds)`, the loop's deliberate pace-holding sleep. The total is closed around the whole iteration by design (:855-857, "the total must cover EVERYTHING").
rows.impact: The whole against which every CPU part is closed is pinned at 1/updateRate by the pacing sleep, not by work. A lever that saves CPU cannot shrink it — the saving migrates into cpu.frame.idle.us, which is counted as a Budget PART of the same whole, so the CPU-domain closure check in telemetry-window.py closes at ~100% no matter what any lever does. That makes the closure oracle unfalsifiable in the Cpu domain (the same "gate that ran, compared nothing, and exited 0" shape), and it makes any "% of frame" figure derived from this whole a ratio against a constant. Combined with #235 (all cpu timers are wall time), a lever's real CPU win is observable in this instrument only as growth in a sleep — which is also the CPU it hands to the server thread and the fidelity governor. The sweeps checked the parts' declarations; nobody checked what the whole physically is.
rows.fixShape: Either exclude cpu.frame.idle.us from the Budget set and declare it Detail (making the unattributed remainder visible and the closure falsifiable), or introduce a work-only whole (total minus idle minus swap-block) as the owner-frame denominator and re-derive the closure against that.
